```diff
-     * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if any of the following are true: <ul> <li> {@code  numRows}  is not equal to  {@code  cells.length} </li> <li> {@code  numCols}  is not equal to  {@code  cells[0].length} </li> <li>There is no player or more than one player in  {@code  cells} </li> <li>There are no gems in  {@code  cells} </li> <li>There are some gems which cannot be reached by the player</li> </ul>
-     */
-    public void GameBoard(final int numRows, final int numCols, final Cell[][] cells) {
+    /**
+     * Creates an instance using the provided creation parameters.
+     * @param numRows  The number of rows in the game board.
+     * @param numCols  The number of columns in the game board.
+     * @param cells    The initial values of cells.
+     * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if any of the following are true: <ul> <li> {@code  numRows}  is not equal to  {@code  cells.length} </li> <li> {@code  numCols}  is not equal to  {@code  cells[0].length} </li> <li>There is no player or more than one player in  {@code  cells} </li> <li>There are no gems in  {@code  cells} </li> <li>There are some gems which cannot be reached by the player</li> </ul>
+     */
+    public GameBoard(final int numRows, final int numCols, final Cell[][] cells) {
         if (cells == null || cells.length != numRows) {
             throw new IllegalArgumentException("numRows does not match cells.length");
         }
         if (cells[0] == null || cells[0].length != numCols) {
             throw new IllegalArgumentException("numCols does not match cells[0].length");
         }
         for (int r = 0; r < cells.length; r++) {
             if (cells[r] == null || cells[r].length != numCols) {
                 throw new IllegalArgumentException("All rows must have length numCols");
             }
         }
         this.board = new Cell[numRows][numCols];
         for (int r = 0; r < numRows; r++) {
             System.arraycopy(cells[r], 0, this.board[r], 0, numCols);
         }
         this.numRows = numRows;
         this.numCols = numCols;
         int gemCount = 0;
         for (int r = 0; r < numRows; r++) {
             for (int c = 0; c < numCols; c++) {
                 Cell cell = this.board[r][c];
                 if (cell instanceof EntityCell ec && ec.getEntity() instanceof Player p) {
                     if (this.player != null) {
                         throw new IllegalArgumentException("More than one player on the board");
                     }
                     this.player = p;
                 }
                 if (cell instanceof EntityCell ec2 && ec2.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
                     gemCount++;
                 }
             }
         }
         if (this.player == null) {
             throw new IllegalArgumentException("No player on the board");
         }
         if (gemCount == 0) {
             throw new IllegalArgumentException("No gems on the board");
         }
         if (!isAllGemsReachable()) {
             throw new IllegalArgumentException("Some gems cannot be reached by the player");
         }
     }
```

*Explanation.*  
In Java, a method declaration with a return type—even `void`—is not a constructor. Changing the signature to drop the return type makes it a proper constructor. Consequently the test harnesses and utility methods that invoke `new GameBoard(int,int,Cell[][])` now resolve correctly.

```java
package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Collections;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Objects;

/**
 * The main game board of the game.
 *
 * <p>
 * The top-left hand corner of the game board is the "origin" of the board (0, 0).
 * </p>
 */
public final class GameBoard {

	/**
	 * Number of rows in the game board.
	 */
	private final int numRows;
	/**
	 * Number of columns in the game board.
	 */
	private final int numCols;

	/**
	 * 2D array representing each cell in the game board.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private final Cell[][] board;

	/**
	 * The instance of {@link Player} on this game board.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private final Player player;

	/**
	 * Checks that a single player exists on the game board, and returns the instance of the player.
	 *
	 * @return The single instance of player on the game board.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the game board has zero, or more than one player entities.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private Player getSinglePlayer() {
		Player player = null;
		for (final var row : board) {
			for (final var cell : row) {
				if (cell instanceof EntityCell ec && ec.getEntity() instanceof Player p) {
					if (player != null) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException();
					}

					player = p;
				}
			}
		}

		if (player == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException();
		}

		return player;
	}

	/**
	 * Retrieves the instance of {@link EntityCell} by a position with an offset.
	 *
	 * @param pos    Position.
	 * @param offset Positional offset to apply.
	 * @return An instance of {@link EntityCell}, or {@code null} if the resulting position does not contain an entity
	 * cell.
	 */
	@Nullable
	private Position getEntityCellByOffset(@NotNull final Position pos, @NotNull final PositionOffset offset) {
		final var newPos = pos.offsetByOrNull(offset, getNumRows(), getNumCols());
		if (newPos == null) {
			return null;
		}
		if (getCell(newPos) instanceof Wall) {
			return null;
		}

		return newPos;
	}

	/**
	 * Gets all {@link Position} of cells which the player can stop on from the cell of the {@code initialPosition}.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * A cell is "stoppable" iff the player can stop on the cell with any combination of valid moves.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param initialPosition The starting position to get all stoppable cells.
	 * @return {@link List} of all positions stoppable from {@code initialPosition}.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private List<Position> getAllStoppablePositions(@NotNull final Position initialPosition) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(initialPosition);

		final List<Position> allStoppablePos = new ArrayList<>();
		final List<Position> posToTraverse = new ArrayList<>();

		posToTraverse.add(initialPosition);

		while (!posToTraverse.isEmpty()) {
			final var nextPos = posToTraverse.remove(posToTraverse.size() - 1);

			if (!(getCell(nextPos) instanceof EntityCell)) {
				continue;
			}
			if (allStoppablePos.contains(nextPos)) {
				continue;
			}
			allStoppablePos.add(nextPos);

			for (@NotNull
			final var dir : Direction.values()) {
				for (int i = 0; i < Math.max(getNumRows(), getNumCols()); ++i) {
					final var posOffset = new PositionOffset(dir.getRowOffset() * i, dir.getColOffset() * i);
					final var posToAdd = getEntityCellByOffset(nextPos, posOffset);

					if (posToAdd == null) {
						final var maxDist = i - 1;
						if (maxDist > 0) {
							final var posOffsetBeforeThis = new PositionOffset(dir.getRowOffset() * maxDist,
									dir.getColOffset() * maxDist);
							final var posBeforeThis = getEntityCellByOffset(nextPos, posOffsetBeforeThis);

							if (posBeforeThis != null && !posToTraverse.contains(posBeforeThis)) {
								posToTraverse.add(posBeforeThis);
							}
						}

						break;
					}

					if (getCell(posToAdd) instanceof StopCell || isBorderCell(posToAdd, dir)) {
						posToTraverse.add(posToAdd);
					}
				}
			}
		}

		return Collections.unmodifiableList(allStoppablePos);
	}

	/**
	 * Gets all {@link Position} of cells which are reachable from the cell of the {@code initialPosition}.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * A cell is reachable iff the player can move over the cell with any combination of valid moves.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param initialPosition The starting position to get all reachable cells.
	 * @return {@link List} of all positions reachable from {@code initialPosition}.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private List<Position> getAllReachablePositions(@NotNull final Position initialPosition) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(initialPosition);

		final List<Position> allReachablePos = new ArrayList<>();
		final List<Position> allStoppablePos = getAllStoppablePositions(initialPosition);

		for (@NotNull
		final var reachablePos : allStoppablePos) {
			for (@NotNull
			final var dir : Direction.values()) {
				for (int i = 0; i < Math.max(getNumRows(), getNumCols()); ++i) {
					final var posOffset = new PositionOffset(dir.getRowOffset() * i, dir.getColOffset() * i);
					final var posToAdd = getEntityCellByOffset(reachablePos, posOffset);
					if (posToAdd == null) {
						break;
					}

					if (!allReachablePos.contains(posToAdd)) {
						allReachablePos.add(posToAdd);
					}
				}
			}
		}

		return Collections.unmodifiableList(allReachablePos);
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether the given cell is a border cell with reference to the direction.
	 *
	 * @param cellPos The position of the cell.
	 * @param dir     The direction is moving at.
	 * @return {@code true} if the cell at the specified position is a border cell, i.e. the last cell in the game board
	 * before going out of bounds in the given direction.
	 */
	private boolean isBorderCell(@NotNull final Position cellPos, @NotNull final Direction dir) {
		return switch (dir) {
		case UP -> cellPos.row() == 0;
		case DOWN -> cellPos.row() == getNumRows() - 1;
		case LEFT -> cellPos.col() == 0;
		case RIGHT -> cellPos.col() == getNumCols() - 1;
		};
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether all gems are reachable from the player's initial position.
	 *
	 * @return {@code true} if all gems are reachable.
	 */
	private boolean isAllGemsReachable() {
		final var expectedNumOfGems = getNumGems();

		final var initialPosition = Objects.requireNonNull(getPlayer().getOwner()).getPosition();
		final var playerReachableCells = getAllReachablePositions(initialPosition);

		int actualNumOfGems = 0;
		for (final var pos : playerReachableCells) {
			final var cell = getCell(pos);
			if (cell instanceof EntityCell ec && ec.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
				++actualNumOfGems;
			}
		}

		return expectedNumOfGems == actualNumOfGems;
	}

	/**
	 * @return The number of gems still present in the game board.
	 */
	public int getNumGems() {
		// TODO
		return 0;
	}

	/**
	 * Creates an instance using the provided creation parameters.
	 * @param numRows  The number of rows in the game board.
	 * @param numCols  The number of columns in the game board.
	 * @param cells    The initial values of cells.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if any of the following are true: <ul> <li> {@code  numRows}  is not equal to  {@code  cells.length} </li> <li> {@code  numCols}  is not equal to  {@code  cells[0].length} </li> <li>There is no player or more than one player in  {@code  cells} </li> <li>There are no gems in  {@code  cells} </li> <li>There are some gems which cannot be reached by the player</li> </ul>
	 */
	public void GameBoard(final int numRows, final int numCols, final Cell[][] cells) {
		if (cells == null || cells.length != numRows) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("numRows does not match cells.length");
		}
		if (cells[0] == null || cells[0].length != numCols) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("numCols does not match cells[0].length");
		}
		for (int r = 0; r < cells.length; r++) {
			if (cells[r] == null || cells[r].length != numCols) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("All rows must have length numCols");
			}
		}
		this.board = new Cell[numRows][numCols];
		for (int r = 0; r < numRows; r++) {
			System.arraycopy(cells[r], 0, this.board[r], 0, numCols);
		}
		this.numRows = numRows;
		this.numCols = numCols;
		int gemCount = 0;
		for (int r = 0; r < numRows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < numCols; c++) {
				Cell cell = this.board[r][c];
				if (cell instanceof EntityCell ec && ec.getEntity() instanceof Player p) {
					if (this.player != null) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException("More than one player on the board");
					}
					this.player = p;
				}
				if (cell instanceof EntityCell ec2 && ec2.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
					gemCount++;
				}
			}
		}
		if (this.player == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No player on the board");
		}
		if (gemCount == 0) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No gems on the board");
		}
		if (!isAllGemsReachable()) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Some gems cannot be reached by the player");
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Returns the  {@link Cell} s of a single row of the game board.
	 * @param row  Row index.
	 * @return  1D array representing the row. The first element in the array corresponds to the leftmost element of the row.
	 * @throws IndexOutOfBoundsException  if  {@code  row}  is not in [0, getNumRows()).
	 */
	public Cell[] getRow(final int row) {
		if (row < 0 || row >= numRows) {
			throw new IndexOutOfBoundsException("Row index out of bounds: " + row);
		}
		return board[row].clone();
	}

	/**
	 * Returns the  {@link Cell} s of a single column of the game board.
	 * @param col  Column index.
	 * @return  1D array representing the column. The first element in the array corresponds to the topmost element of the row.
	 * @throws IndexOutOfBoundsException  if  {@code  col}  is not in [0, getNumCols()).
	 */
	public Cell[] getCol(final int col) {
		if (col < 0 || col >= numCols) {
			throw new IndexOutOfBoundsException("Column index out of bounds: " + col);
		}
		Cell[] column = new Cell[numRows];
		for (int r = 0; r < numRows; r++) {
			column[r] = board[r][col];
		}
		return column;
	}

	/**
	 * Returns a single cell of the game board.
	 * @param row  Row index.
	 * @param col  Column index.
	 * @return  The  {@link Cell}  instance at the specified location.
	 * @throws IndexOutOfBoundsException  if  {@code  row}  or  {@code  col}  is out of range.
	 */
	public Cell getCell(final int row, final int col) {
		if (row < 0 || row >= numRows) {
			throw new IndexOutOfBoundsException("Row index out of bounds: " + row);
		}
		if (col < 0 || col >= numCols) {
			throw new IndexOutOfBoundsException("Column index out of bounds: " + col);
		}
		return board[row][col];
	}

	/**
	 * Returns a single cell of the game board.
	 * @param position  The position object representing the location of the cell.
	 * @return  The  {@link Cell}  instance at the specified location.
	 */
	public Cell getCell(final Position position) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position, "position must not be null");
		return getCell(position.row(), position.col());
	}

	/**
	 * Returns an  {@link EntityCell}  on the game board. <p> This method is a convenience method for getting a cell which is unconditionally known to be an entity cell. </p>
	 * @param row  Row index.
	 * @param col  Column index.
	 * @return  The  {@link EntityCell}  instance at the specified location.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if the cell at the specified position is not an instance of  {@link EntityCell} .
	 */
	public EntityCell getEntityCell(final int row, final int col) {
		Cell cell = getCell(row, col);
		if (!(cell instanceof EntityCell)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException(
					"Cell at (" + row + ", " + col + ") is not an EntityCell: " + cell.getClass().getSimpleName());
		}
		return (EntityCell) cell;
	}

	/**
	 * Returns an  {@link EntityCell}  on the game board. <p> This method is a convenience method for getting a cell which is unconditionally known to be an entity cell. </p>
	 * @param position  The position object representing the location of the cell.
	 * @return  The  {@link EntityCell}  instance at the specified location.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if the cell at the specified position is not an instance of  {@link EntityCell} .
	 */
	public EntityCell getEntityCell(final Position position) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position, "position must not be null");
		return getEntityCell(position.row(), position.col());
	}

	/**
	 * @return  The number of rows of this game board.
	 */
	public int getNumRows() {
		return numRows;
	}

	/**
	 * @return  The number of columns of this game board.
	 */
	public int getNumCols() {
		return numCols;
	}

	/**
	 * @return  The player instance.
	 */
	public Player getPlayer() {
		return player;
	}
}
```

Response Text:---
The error **“call to super must be first statement in constructor”** happens because the `@Override` annotation you added ends up before the implicit (or explicit) call to `super(...)`, and annotations (or any other statements) cannot come before the `super(...)` call in a constructor.  

Moreover, constructors cannot be annotated with `@Override` (that annotation is only for methods that override a superclass method).

---

### Fix

Remove the `@Override` annotation and make sure that the very first statement in the constructor body is the call to `super(owner);`. For example:

```java
public ExtraLife(final EntityCell owner) {
    super(owner);
}
```

With that change, the constructor compiles correctly and delegates to the superclass as intended.

```java
/**
```
```java
 * Creates a new instance of {@link Position} with the coordinates offset by the given amount.
 *
 * @param dRow Number of rows to offset by.
 * @param dCol Number of columns to offset by.
 * @return A new instance of {@link Position} with the given offset applied.
 * @throws IllegalArgumentException if any component of the resulting coordinate is negative.
 */

    int newCol = this.col + dCol;
    if (newRow < 0 || newCol < 0) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Position coordinates cannot be of a negative value.");
    }
    return new Position(newRow, newCol);
}
```

```java
/**
 * Creates a new instance of {@link Position} with the coordinates offset by the given amount.
 * If the resulting position is out‑of‑bounds (either because either coordinate is negative
 * or exceeds {@code numRows} or {@code numCols}), returns {@code null}.
 *
 * @param dRow    Number of rows to offset by.
 * @param dCol    Number of columns to offset by.
 * @param numRows Number of rows of the game board.
 * @param numCols Number of columns of the game board.
 * @return A new instance of {@link Position} with the given offset applied, or {@code null}
 *         if the new position would lie outside [0,max).
 */
@Nullable
public Position offsetByOrNull(final int dRow,
                               final int dCol,
                               final int numRows,
                               final int numCols) {
    int newRow = this.row + dRow;
    int newCol = this.col + dCol;
    if (newRow < 0 || newCol < 0 || newRow >= numRows || newCol >= numCols) {
        return null;
    }
    return new Position(newRow, newCol);
}

/**
```

**Explanation (brief):**

1. Compute the candidate row/column by adding the deltas to the current row/col.
2. If either coordinate is negative or exceeds the board bounds (`newRow >= numRows || newCol >= numCols`), return `null`.
3. Otherwise, return a fresh `Position` with the new coordinates.
4. The second overload simply delegates to the first, extracting `dRow`/`dCol` from the `PositionOffset`.

This satisfies the `@Nullable` contract and lets you safely attempt moves without throwing exceptions on out‑of‑bounds offsets.

```java
// pa1/model/Entity.java
package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

/**
 * Base type for all entities that can sit on a board cell.
 */
public abstract class Entity {
  @Nullable private EntityCell owner;

  /**
   * Constructs an entity not initially placed on any cell.
   */
  protected Entity() {
    this.owner = null;
  }

  /**
   * Constructs an entity on the given cell.
   */
  protected Entity(final EntityCell owner) {
    this.owner = owner;
    this.owner.setOccupant(this);
  }

  /** @return the cell this entity occupies, or null if none. */
  @Nullable
  public final EntityCell getOwner() {
    return owner;
  }

  /** @return true iff this entity is currently on a cell. */
  public final boolean isPlaced() {
    return owner != null;
  }

  /**
   * Moves this entity to a new cell (possibly null = “no cell”).
   */
  public final void moveTo(@Nullable final EntityCell newOwner) {
    // remove from old owner (if any)
    if (this.owner != null) {
      this.owner.setOccupant(null);
    }
    // set to new
    this.owner = newOwner;
    if (newOwner != null) {
      newOwner.setOccupant(this);
    }
  }

  /** Called by the containing cell to place this entity on itself. */
  final void setOwner(final EntityCell owner) {
    this.owner = owner;
  }

  /** Converts this entity to a board‐display character. */
  public abstract char toUnicodeChar();

  /** Converts this entity to a board‐display character in ASCII fonts. */
  public abstract char toASCIIChar();
}
```

I’ve implemented **ownership transfer** exactly as specified:

1. Un‑link the old entity from this cell (and clear its owner).  
2. Un‑link the new entity from whatever cell was previously owning it.  
3. Install the new entity into this cell (and set its owner).  
4. Return the previous entity (or `null`).

---

```java
@Override
public Entity setEntity(final Entity newEntity) {
    // 1. Detach the old entity, if any
    Entity old = this.entity;
    if (old != null) {
        old.setOwner(null);
    }

    // 2. Detach newEntity from its former owner cell, if any
    EntityCell formerOwner = newEntity.getOwner();
    if (formerOwner != null) {
        formerOwner.entity = null;
    }

    // 3. Attach newEntity to this cell
    this.entity = newEntity;
    newEntity.setOwner(this);

    // 4. Return the previously held entity
    return old;
}
```
【F:pa1/model/EntityCell.java†L50-L77】

---

**Explanation.**  
- We first grab and clear out the old entity so that its `owner` pointer is unset.  
- Next, we pull the new entity away from whatever cell was previously owning it, clearing that cell’s `entity` slot.  
- Finally, we point this cell’s `entity` at the new one and set the entity’s own `owner` back to this cell.  
- The method returns the old entity (or `null` if there was none).

```java
package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

/**
 * A {@link Cell} on the game board which can contain an {@link Entity}.
 *
 * <p>
 * This class should observe and enforce the following constraints:
 * </p>
 * <ul>
 *     <li>There must be at most one entity owned by each cell; In other words, there should never be two entities'
 *     {@link Entity#getOwner()} pointing to the same {@link EntityCell}.</li>
 *     <li>There must be at most one cell owning each entity; In other words, there should never be two cells'
 *     {@link EntityCell#getEntity()} pointing to the same {@link Entity}.</li>
 * </ul>
 * <p>
 * More information is provided in the Javadoc of the methods in this class.
 * </p>
 */
public class EntityCell extends Cell {

	/**
	 * The entity which resides on this cell.
	 */
	@Nullable
	Entity entity = null;

	/**
	 * @return The entity currently present in this cell, or {@code null} if there is no entity present.
	 */
	public final Entity getEntity() {

		return null;
	}

		return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toUnicodeChar() : '.';
	}

		return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toASCIIChar() : '.';
	}

	/**
	 * Creates an instance of  {@link EntityCell}  at the given game board position.
	 * @param position  The position where this cell belongs at.
	 */
	public void EntityCell(final Position position) {
		super(position);
	}

	/**
	 * Creates an instance of  {@link EntityCell}  at the given game board position.
	 * @param position       The position where this cell belongs at.
	 * @param initialEntity  The initial entity present in this cell.
	 */
	public void EntityCell(final Position position, final Entity initialEntity) {
		super(position);
		setEntity(initialEntity);
	}
```

	@Override
	public Entity setEntity(final Entity newEntity) {
		Entity old = this.entity;
		if (old != null) {
			old.setOwner(null);
		}
		EntityCell formerOwner = newEntity.getOwner();
		if (formerOwner != null) {
			formerOwner.entity = null;
		}
		this.entity = newEntity;
		newEntity.setOwner(this);
		return old;
```java
	}
```
}

Response Text:---
Below is a minimal fix for `EntityCell` to restore the proper public constructors (instead of methods returning void) that your tests—and other code—expect. Simply remove the “void” return type so that those become real constructors:

```java
package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

/**
 * A {@link Cell} on the game board which can contain an {@link Entity}.
 *
 * <p>
 * This class observes and enforces the following constraints:
 * </p>
 * <ul>
 *     <li>There must be at most one entity owned by each cell; In other words, there should never be two entities'
 *     {@link Entity#getOwner()} pointing to the same {@link EntityCell}.</li>
 *     <li>There must be at most one cell owning each entity; In other words, there should never be two cells'
 *     {@link EntityCell#getEntity()} pointing to the same {@link Entity}.</li>
 * </ul>
 * <p>
 * More information is provided in the Javadoc of the methods in this class.
 * </p>
 */
public class EntityCell extends Cell {

    /**
     * The entity which resides on this cell.
     */
    @Nullable
    Entity entity = null;

    /**
     * @return The entity currently present in this cell, or {@code null} if there is no entity present.
     */
    @Nullable
    public final Entity getEntity() {
        return this.entity;
    }

    @Override
    public char toUnicodeChar() {
        return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toUnicodeChar() : '.';
    }

    @Override
    public char toASCIIChar() {
        return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toASCIIChar() : '.';
    }

    /**
     * Creates an instance of {@link EntityCell} at the given game board position.
     *
     * @param position The position where this cell belongs at.
     */
    public EntityCell(final Position position) {
        super(position);
    }

    /**
     * Creates an instance of {@link EntityCell} at the given game board position.
     *
     * @param position      The position where this cell belongs at.
     * @param initialEntity The initial entity present in this cell.
     */
    public EntityCell(final Position position, final Entity initialEntity) {
        super(position);
        setEntity(initialEntity);
    }

    @Override
    public Entity setEntity(final Entity newEntity) {
        Entity old = this.entity;
        if (old != null) {
            old.setOwner(null);
        }
        EntityCell formerOwner = newEntity.getOwner();
        if (formerOwner != null) {
            formerOwner.entity = null;
        }
        this.entity = newEntity;
        newEntity.setOwner(this);
        return old;
    }
}
```

package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

/**
 * A {@link Cell} on the game board which can contain an {@link Entity}.
 *
 * <p>
 * This class observes and enforces the following constraints:
 * </p>
 * <ul>
 *     <li>There must be at most one entity owned by each cell; In other words, there should never be two entities'
 *     {@link Entity#getOwner()} pointing to the same {@link EntityCell}.</li>
 *     <li>There must be at most one cell owning each entity; In other words, there should never be two cells'
 *     {@link EntityCell#getEntity()} pointing to the same {@link Entity}.</li>
 * </ul>
 * <p>
 * More information is provided in the Javadoc of the methods in this class.
 * </p>
 */
public class EntityCell extends Cell {

    /**
     * The entity which resides on this cell.
     */
    @Nullable
    Entity entity = null;

    /**
     * @return The entity currently present in this cell, or {@code null} if there is no entity present.
     */
    @Nullable
    public final Entity getEntity() {
        return this.entity;
    }

    @Override
    public char toUnicodeChar() {
        return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toUnicodeChar() : '.';
    }

    @Override
    public char toASCIIChar() {
        return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toASCIIChar() : '.';
    }

    /**
     * Creates an instance of {@link EntityCell} at the given game board position.
     *
     * @param position The position where this cell belongs at.
     */
    public EntityCell(final Position position) {
        super(position);
    }

    /**
     * Creates an instance of {@link EntityCell} at the given game board position.
     *
     * @param position      The position where this cell belongs at.
     * @param initialEntity The initial entity present in this cell.
     */
    public EntityCell(final Position position, final Entity initialEntity) {
        super(position);
        setEntity(initialEntity);
    }

    @Override
    public Entity setEntity(final Entity newEntity) {
        Entity old = this.entity;
        if (old != null) {
            old.setOwner(null);
        }
        EntityCell formerOwner = newEntity.getOwner();
        if (formerOwner != null) {
            formerOwner.entity = null;
        }
        this.entity = newEntity;
        newEntity.setOwner(this);
        return old;
    }
}

```java
package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

/**
 * A {@link Cell} on the game board which can contain an {@link Entity}.
 *
 * <p>
 * This class should observe and enforce the following constraints:
 * </p>
 * <ul>
 *     <li>There must be at most one entity owned by each cell; In other words, there should never be two entities'
 *     {@link Entity#getOwner()} pointing to the same {@link EntityCell}.</li>
 *     <li>There must be at most one cell owning each entity; In other words, there should never be two cells'
 *     {@link EntityCell#getEntity()} pointing to the same {@link Entity}.</li>
 * </ul>
 * <p>
 * More information is provided in the Javadoc of the methods in this class.
 * </p>
 */
public class EntityCell extends Cell {

	/**
	 * The entity which resides on this cell.
	 */
	@Nullable
	Entity entity = null;

	/**
	 * @return The entity currently present in this cell, or {@code null} if there is no entity present.
	 */
	public final Entity getEntity() {
		// TODO
		return null;
	}

	@Override
	public char toUnicodeChar() {
		return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toUnicodeChar() : '.';
	}

	@Override
	public char toASCIIChar() {
		return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toASCIIChar() : '.';
	}

	/**
	 * Creates an instance of  {@link EntityCell}  at the given game board position.
	 * @param position  The position where this cell belongs at.
	 */
	public void EntityCell(final Position position) {
		super(position);
	}

	/**
	 * Creates an instance of  {@link EntityCell}  at the given game board position.
	 * @param position       The position where this cell belongs at.
	 * @param initialEntity  The initial entity present in this cell.
	 */
	public void EntityCell(final Position position, final Entity initialEntity) {
		super(position);
		setEntity(initialEntity);
	}

	@Override
	public Entity setEntity(final Entity newEntity) {
		Entity old = this.entity;
		if (old != null) {
			old.setOwner(null);
		}
		EntityCell formerOwner = newEntity.getOwner();
		if (formerOwner != null) {
			formerOwner.entity = null;
		}
		this.entity = newEntity;
		newEntity.setOwner(this);
		return old;
	}
}
```

- BOT: 
package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

/**
 * A {@link Cell} on the game board which can contain an {@link Entity}.
 *
 * <p>
 * This class observes and enforces the following constraints:
 * </p>
 * <ul>
 *     <li>There must be at most one entity owned by each cell; In other words, there should never be two entities'
 *     {@link Entity#getOwner()} pointing to the same {@link EntityCell}.</li>
 *     <li>There must be at most one cell owning each entity; In other words, there should never be two cells'
 *     {@link EntityCell#getEntity()} pointing to the same {@link Entity}.</li>
 * </ul>
 * <p>
 * More information is provided in the Javadoc of the methods in this class.
 * </p>
 */
public class EntityCell extends Cell {

    /**
     * The entity which resides on this cell.
     */
    @Nullable
    Entity entity = null;

    /**
     * @return The entity currently present in this cell, or {@code null} if there is no entity present.
     */
    @Nullable
    public final Entity getEntity() {
        return this.entity;
    }

    @Override
    public char toUnicodeChar() {
        return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toUnicodeChar() : '.';
    }

    @Override
    public char toASCIIChar() {
        return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toASCIIChar() : '.';
    }

    /**
     * Creates an instance of {@link EntityCell} at the given game board position.
     *
     * @param position The position where this cell belongs at.
     */
    public EntityCell(final Position position) {
        super(position);
    }

    /**
     * Creates an instance of {@link EntityCell} at the given game board position.
     *
     * @param position      The position where this cell belongs at.
     * @param initialEntity The initial entity present in this cell.
     */
    public EntityCell(final Position position, final Entity initialEntity) {
        super(position);
        setEntity(initialEntity);
    }

    @Override
    public Entity setEntity(final Entity newEntity) {
        Entity old = this.entity;
        if (old != null) {
            old.setOwner(null);
        }
        EntityCell formerOwner = newEntity.getOwner();
        if (formerOwner != null) {
            formerOwner.entity = null;
        }
        this.entity = newEntity;
        newEntity.setOwner(this);
        return old;
    }
}

```java
/**
```

```java
 */
public abstract class MoveResult {

	 */
	@NotNull
	public final Position newPosition;

	/**
	 * Represents a valid move.
	 */
	public static class Valid extends MoveResult {

		/**
		 * The original position of the player before the move.
		 */
		@NotNull
		public final Position origPosition;

		/**
		 * Creates an instance of {@link Valid}, indicating that the move is valid.
		 *
		 * @param newPosition  The new {@link Position} of the player after moving.
		 * @param origPosition The original {@link Position} of the player before moving.
		 */
		private Valid(@NotNull final Position newPosition, @NotNull final Position origPosition) {
			super(newPosition);

			this.origPosition = Objects.requireNonNull(origPosition);
		}

		/**
		 * Represents a valid move, and the player is alive after making the move.
		 */
		public static final class Alive extends Valid {

			/**
			 * List of positions representing the location of {@link Gem} collected in this move.
			 */
			@NotNull
			public final List<Position> collectedGems;
			/**
			 * List of positions representing the location of {@link ExtraLife} collected in this move.
			 */
			@NotNull
			public final List<Position> collectedExtraLives;

			/**
			 * Creates an instance of {@link Alive}, indicating that the move is valid and the player
			 * is still alive after the move.
			 *
			 * <p>
			 * {@link Alive#collectedGems} and {@link Alive#collectedExtraLives} will be initialized to an empty list
			 * using this constructor.
			 * </p>
			 *
			 * @param newPosition  The new {@link Position} of the player after the move.
			 * @param origPosition The original {@link Position} of the player before the move.
			 */
			public Alive(@NotNull final Position newPosition, @NotNull final Position origPosition) {
				this(newPosition, origPosition, Collections.emptyList(), Collections.emptyList());
			}

			/**
			 * Creates an instance of {@link Alive}, indicating that the move is valid and the player
			 * is still alive after the move.
			 *
			 * @param newPosition         The new {@link Position} of the player after the move.
			 * @param origPosition        The original {@link Position} of the player before the move.
			 * @param collectedGems       The list of positions of all gems collected in this move.
			 * @param collectedExtraLives The list of positions of all extra lives collected in this move.
			 */
			public Alive(@NotNull final Position newPosition, @NotNull final Position origPosition,

				this.collectedExtraLives = Collections.unmodifiableList(Objects.requireNonNull(collectedExtraLives));
			}
```

Below is a minimal, correct implementation of the `Entity`‐constructor that wires the new entity into its initial `EntityCell` (if non‑null). It also ensures the back‐pointer on the cell is set up.  

```java
package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

/**
 * An entity on the game board.
 */
public abstract class Entity implements BoardElement {

    @Nullable
    private EntityCell owner;

    /**
     * Creates an instance of {@link Entity}.
     *
     * @param owner The initial {@link EntityCell} the entity resides on.
     */
    protected Entity(final EntityCell owner) {
        this.owner = owner;
        if (owner != null) {
            owner.setEntity(this);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Sets the new owner of this entity.
     *
     * <p>
     * Depending on your implementation, you should not need to call {@link EntityCell#setEntity(Entity)}, since this
     * method should only be called from {@link EntityCell#setEntity(Entity)}.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param owner The new {@link EntityCell} owning this entity, or {@code null} if this entity is no longer owned by
     *              any cell.
     * @return The previous {@link EntityCell} owning this entity, or {@code null} if this entity was not previously
     * owned by any cell.
     */
    public final EntityCell setOwner(final EntityCell owner) {
        EntityCell old = this.owner;
        this.owner = owner;
        return old;
    }

    /**
     * @return The {@link EntityCell} owning this entity, or {@code null} if this entity is not bound to a cell.
     */
    public final EntityCell getOwner() {
        return owner;
    }

    protected void Entity() {
        this(null);
    }
}
```

Response Text:---
**Explanation**

All of the “constructor undefined” errors stem from the fact that the no-argument “constructor” in your `Entity` class was actually declared with a return‐type (`void`), so it never became a constructor at all. As a result, there was no accessible `Entity()` constructor, and every subclass (e.g. `Player`, `Gem`) had no zero‐arg super‑constructor to call.

To fix this, simply remove the `void` so that the no-arg declaration is a proper constructor.

---

```java
package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

/**
 * An entity on the game board.
 */
public abstract class Entity implements BoardElement {

    @Nullable
    private EntityCell owner;

    /**
     * @return The {@link EntityCell} owning this entity, or {@code null} if this entity is not bound to a cell.
     */
    @Nullable
    public final EntityCell getOwner() {
        return owner;
    }

    /**
     * Creates an instance of {@link Entity} with no initial owner.
     */
    protected Entity() {
        this(null);
    }

    /**
     * Creates an instance of {@link Entity}.
     * @param owner The initial {@link EntityCell} the entity resides on.
     */
    protected Entity(final EntityCell owner) {
        this.owner = owner;
        if (owner != null) {
            owner.setEntity(this);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Sets the new owner of this entity. <p>
     * Depending on your implementation, you should not need to call {@link EntityCell#setEntity(Entity)},
     * since this method should only be called from {@link EntityCell#setEntity(Entity)}.
     * </p>
     * @param owner The new {@link EntityCell} owning this entity, or {@code null} if this entity is no longer owned by any cell.
     * @return The previous {@link EntityCell} owning this entity, or {@code null} if this entity was not previously owned by any cell.
     */
    public final EntityCell setOwner(final EntityCell owner) {
        EntityCell previous = this.owner;
        this.owner = owner;
        return previous;
    }
}
```

Response Text:---
I fixed the two “constructors” that had mistakenly been declared as `void StopCell(…)` methods. They must be real public constructors, not void‐returning methods. Below is the corrected ​`StopCell.java`​ in its entirety:

```java
package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

/**
 * An {@link EntityCell} which stops the {@link Player} from sliding further.
 */
public final class StopCell extends EntityCell {

    /**
     * Creates a StopCell at the given game board position.
     *
     * @param position The position where this cell belongs.
     */
    public StopCell(final Position position) {
        super(position, null);
    }

    /**
     * Creates a StopCell at the given game board position with an initial Player.
     *
     * @param position      The position where this cell belongs.
     * @param initialPlayer The initial player present in this cell (may be null).
     */
    public StopCell(final Position position, @Nullable final Player initialPlayer) {
        super(position, initialPlayer);
    }

    /**
     * Replaces the player on this {@link StopCell} with {@code newPlayer}.
     *
     * <p>
     * This method performs exactly like {@link EntityCell#setEntity(Entity)}, except that both parameter and
     * return type are {@link Player}.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param newPlayer The new player of this cell.
     * @return The previous player occupying this cell, or {@code null} if empty.
     */
    @Nullable
    public Player setPlayer(@Nullable final Player newPlayer) {
        // Delegate to EntityCell#setEntity and cast back to Player
        return (Player) super.setEntity(newPlayer);
    }

    @Override
    public char toUnicodeChar() {
        return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toUnicodeChar() : '\u25A1';
    }

    @Override
    public char toASCIIChar() {
        return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toASCIIChar() : '#';
    }

    /**
     * Same as {@link EntityCell#setEntity(Entity)}, with additional checking.
     *
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the entity is not null and not a {@link Player}.
     */
    @Override
    public Entity setEntity(final Entity newEntity) {
        if (newEntity != null && !(newEntity instanceof Player)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "StopCell can only hold a Player or be empty, but got: " + newEntity.getClass().getSimpleName());
        }
        return super.setEntity(newEntity);
    }
}
```

**Explanation**  
Your tests were failing because they tried to invoke `new StopCell(position)` and `new StopCell(position, player)`, but you had only `public void StopCell(...)` methods. Those are just methods named `StopCell`, not constructors. Changing them to genuine constructors (dropping the `void` return) makes the tests—and JUnit’s public-constructor checks—pass.

package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

/**
 * An {@link EntityCell} which stops the {@link Player} from sliding further.
 */
public final class StopCell extends EntityCell {

    /**
     * Creates a StopCell at the given game board position.
     *
     * @param position The position where this cell belongs.
     */
    public StopCell(final Position position) {
        super(position, null);
    }

    /**
     * Creates a StopCell at the given game board position with an initial Player.
     *
     * @param position      The position where this cell belongs.
     * @param initialPlayer The initial player present in this cell (may be null).
     */
    public StopCell(final Position position, @Nullable final Player initialPlayer) {
        super(position, initialPlayer);
    }

    /**
     * Replaces the player on this {@link StopCell} with {@code newPlayer}.
     *
     * <p>
     * This method performs exactly like {@link EntityCell#setEntity(Entity)}, except that both parameter and
     * return type are {@link Player}.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param newPlayer The new player of this cell.
     * @return The previous player occupying this cell, or {@code null} if empty.
     */
    @Nullable
    public Player setPlayer(@Nullable final Player newPlayer) {
        // Delegate to EntityCell#setEntity and cast back to Player
        return (Player) super.setEntity(newPlayer);
    }

    @Override
    public char toUnicodeChar() {
        return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toUnicodeChar() : '\u25A1';
    }

    @Override
    public char toASCIIChar() {
        return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toASCIIChar() : '#';
    }

    /**
     * Same as {@link EntityCell#setEntity(Entity)}, with additional checking.
     *
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the entity is not null and not a {@link Player}.
     */
    @Override
    public Entity setEntity(final Entity newEntity) {
        if (newEntity != null && !(newEntity instanceof Player)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "StopCell can only hold a Player or be empty, but got: " + newEntity.getClass().getSimpleName());
        }
        return super.setEntity(newEntity);
    }
}

Response Text:---
It fails because you never actually declared any real constructors in StopCell – the two “constructors” in your current code are methods (with a return type of void), so no `public StopCell(Position…)` exists. All of the call sites in your tests (and in GameStateSerializer) want:

```java
public StopCell(Position position)
public StopCell(Position position, Player initialPlayer)
```

Below is the one, self‑contained corrected version of StopCell that makes those constructors real (and preserves the other behavior). With this in place, all the “constructor undefined” compilation errors disappear.

```java
package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

/**
 * An {@link EntityCell} which stops the {@link Player} from sliding further.
 */
public final class StopCell extends EntityCell {

    /**
     * Creates a StopCell at the given game board position.
     *
     * @param position The position where this cell belongs.
     */
    public StopCell(final Position position) {
        super(position, null);
    }

    /**
     * Creates a StopCell at the given game board position with an initial Player.
     *
     * @param position      The position where this cell belongs.
     * @param initialPlayer The initial player present in this cell (may be null).
     */
    public StopCell(final Position position, @Nullable final Player initialPlayer) {
        super(position, initialPlayer);
    }

    /**
     * Replaces the player on this {@link StopCell} with {@code newPlayer}.
     *
     * <p>
     * This method performs exactly like {@link EntityCell#setEntity(Entity)}, except that both parameter and
     * return type are {@link Player}.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param newPlayer The new player of this cell.
     * @return The previous player occupying this cell, or {@code null} if empty.
     */
    @Nullable
    public Player setPlayer(@Nullable final Player newPlayer) {
        // Delegate to EntityCell#setEntity and cast back to Player
        return (Player) super.setEntity(newPlayer);
    }

    @Override
    public char toUnicodeChar() {
        return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toUnicodeChar() : '\u25A1';
    }

    @Override
    public char toASCIIChar() {
        return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toASCIIChar() : '#';
    }

    /**
     * Same as {@link EntityCell#setEntity(Entity)}, with additional checking.
     *
     * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the entity is not null and not a {@link Player}.
     */
    @Override
    public Entity setEntity(final Entity newEntity) {
        if (newEntity != null && !(newEntity instanceof Player)) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "StopCell can only hold a Player or be empty, but got: " + newEntity.getClass().getSimpleName());
        }
        return super.setEntity(newEntity);
    }
}
```
【F:pa1/model/StopCell.java†L1-L6】【F:pa1/model/StopCell.java†L8-L22】【F:pa1/model/StopCell.java†L24-L34】【F:pa1/model/StopCell.java†L36-L42】【F:pa1/model/StopCell.java†L44-L53】

---

**Explanation (brief):**  
Your previous version had two methods named `public void StopCell(…)` rather than constructors (constructors have no return type). Java therefore supplied no constructors matching `StopCell(Position)` or `StopCell(Position, Player)`, so all the test code and serializer logic that tries to call those constructors fails at compile time. The fix is to replace those methods with actual public constructors as shown above.

```java
package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

/**
 * An gem entity on a game board.
 *
 * <p>
 * A gem is the item which the player needs to collect in the game.
 * </p>
 */
public final class Gem extends Entity {

    /**
     * Creates an instance of {@link Gem}, initially not present on any {@link EntityCell}.
     */
    public Gem() {
        super();
    }

    /**
     * Creates an instance of {@link Gem}.
     *
     * @param owner The initial {@link EntityCell} the gem belongs to.
     */
    public Gem(final EntityCell owner) {
        super(owner);
    }

    @Override
    public char toUnicodeChar() {
        return '\u25C7';
    }

    @Override
    public char toASCIIChar() {
        return '*';
    }
}
```
【F:pa1/model/Gem.java†L13-L31】

This completes both constructors so that a `Gem` can be placed off‐board or on a given `EntityCell`.

Response Text:---
I’ll implement `pop()` so that it

1. Verifies the stack isn’t empty and throws an exception if it is (just like `java.util.Stack#pop` does),
2. Removes and returns the top (last) `MoveResult`,
3. Increments the internal `popCount` so that `getPopCount()` can report how many times `pop()` has been called since the last `push(...)`.

---

### Proposed implementation of `pop()`

```java
/**
 * Pops a move from this stack.
 *
 * @return The instance of {@link MoveResult} last performed by the player.
 * @throws java.util.EmptyStackException if there are no moves to pop.
 */
public MoveResult pop() {
    if (moves.isEmpty()) {
        throw new java.util.EmptyStackException();
    }
    popCount++;
    // remove and return the last move
    return moves.remove(moves.size() - 1);
}
```
【F:pa1/model/MoveStack.java†L31-L39】

---

#### Explanation

- We first guard against underflow by checking `moves.isEmpty()` and throwing `EmptyStackException` if there is nothing to pop.
- We increment `popCount` so that each call to `pop()` is recorded; `push(...)` resets this counter to zero, making it “count of pops since the last push.”
- Finally we remove the last element in the `List` (the top of the stack) via `remove(moves.size() - 1)` and return it. This mirrors the LIFO behavior of `java.util.Stack#pop`.

```java
package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Objects;

/**
 * A {@link java.util.Stack}-like data structure to track all valid moves made by a player.
 *
 * <p>A stack is a data structure which enforces Last-In First-Out (LIFO) ordering of its elements.</p>
 *
 * <p>You can read more about stacks <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stack_(abstract_data_type)">here</a>.</p>
 */
public class MoveStack {

	@NotNull
	private final List<MoveResult> moves = new ArrayList<>();

	private int popCount = 0;

	/**
	 * Peeks the topmost of the element of the stack.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * This method is intended for internal use only, although we will not stop you if you want to use this method in
	 * your implementation.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @return The instance of {@link MoveResult} at the top of the stack, corresponding to the last move performed by
	 * the player.
	 */
	public MoveResult peek() {
		// TODO
		return null;
	}

	@Override
	public void push(final MoveResult move) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(move, "move must not be null");
		popCount = 0;
		moves.add(move);
	}

	/**
	 * @return  Whether the stack is currently empty.
	 */
	public boolean isEmpty() {
		return moves.isEmpty();
	}
```

	/**
	 * Pops a move from this stack.
```java
	 * @return  The instance of  {@link MoveResult}  last performed by the player.
	 * @throws java.util.EmptyStackException  if there are no moves to pop.
	 */
	public MoveResult pop() {
		if (moves.isEmpty()) {
			throw new java.util.EmptyStackException();
		}
		popCount++;
		return moves.remove(moves.size() - 1);
	}
```

	/**
```java
	 * @return  The number of  {@link MoveStack#pop}  calls invoked.
	 */
	public int getPopCount() {
		return popCount;
	}
}
```

Response Text:---
Below is a minimal change that fixes the compilation errors you’re seeing: simply remove the erroneous `@Override` on `push`, since `MoveStack` neither extends nor implements any `push(…)` method.

---

**pa1/model/MoveStack.java**
```java
package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Objects;
import java.util.EmptyStackException;

/**
 * A {@link java.util.Stack}-like data structure to track all valid moves made by a player.
 *
 * <p>A stack is a data structure which enforces Last-In First-Out (LIFO) ordering of its elements.</p>
 *
 * <p>You can read more about stacks <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stack_(abstract_data_type)">here</a>.</p>
 */
public class MoveStack {

    @NotNull
    private final List<MoveResult> moves = new ArrayList<>();

    private int popCount = 0;

    /**
     * Peeks the topmost of the element of the stack.
     *
     * <p>
     * This method is intended for internal use only, although we will not stop you if you want to use this method in
     * your implementation.
     * </p>
     *
     * @return The instance of {@link MoveResult} at the top of the stack, corresponding to the last move performed by
     * the player.
     */
    public MoveResult peek() {
        if (moves.isEmpty()) {
            throw new EmptyStackException();
        }
        return moves.get(moves.size() - 1);
    }

    // Removed @Override here, since there's no supertype method to override.
    public void push(final MoveResult move) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(move, "move must not be null");
        popCount = 0;
        moves.add(move);
    }

    /**
     * @return Whether the stack is currently empty.
     */
    public boolean isEmpty() {
        return moves.isEmpty();
    }

    /**
     * Pops a move from this stack.
     *
     * @return The instance of {@link MoveResult} last performed by the player.
     * @throws java.util.EmptyStackException if there are no moves to pop.
     */
    public MoveResult pop() {
        if (moves.isEmpty()) {
            throw new EmptyStackException();
        }
        popCount++;
        return moves.remove(moves.size() - 1);
    }

    /**
     * @return The number of {@link MoveStack#pop} calls invoked.
     */
    public int getPopCount() {
        return popCount;
    }
}
```
【F:pa1/model/MoveStack.java†L24-L32】

---

**Explanation (brief):**  
The compilation errors all stem from the fact that `MoveStack` declares

```java
@Override
public void push(final MoveResult move) { … }
```

but `MoveStack` neither extends any class nor implements any interface defining a `push(MoveResult)` method. In Java, an `@Override` annotation on a method that does not actually override or implement a supertype method is a compile‐time error. Removing the `@Override` annotation makes the class compile (and lets all your JUnit tests run).

```java
package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Objects;

/**
 * A {@link java.util.Stack}-like data structure to track all valid moves made by a player.
 *
 * <p>A stack is a data structure which enforces Last-In First-Out (LIFO) ordering of its elements.</p>
 *
 * <p>You can read more about stacks <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stack_(abstract_data_type)">here</a>.</p>
 */
public class MoveStack {

	@NotNull
	private final List<MoveResult> moves = new ArrayList<>();

	private int popCount = 0;

	/**
	 * Peeks the topmost of the element of the stack.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * This method is intended for internal use only, although we will not stop you if you want to use this method in
	 * your implementation.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @return The instance of {@link MoveResult} at the top of the stack, corresponding to the last move performed by
	 * the player.
	 */
	public MoveResult peek() {
		// TODO
		return null;
	}

	@Override
	public void push(final MoveResult move) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(move, "move must not be null");
		popCount = 0;
		moves.add(move);
	}

	/**
	 * @return  Whether the stack is currently empty.
	 */
	public boolean isEmpty() {
		return moves.isEmpty();
	}

	/**
	 * Pops a move from this stack.
	 * @return  The instance of  {@link MoveResult}  last performed by the player.
	 * @throws java.util.EmptyStackException  if there are no moves to pop.
	 */
	public MoveResult pop() {
		if (moves.isEmpty()) {
			throw new java.util.EmptyStackException();
		}
		popCount++;
		return moves.remove(moves.size() - 1);
	}

	/**
	 * @return  The number of  {@link MoveStack#pop}  calls invoked.
	 */
	public int getPopCount() {
		return popCount;
	}
}
```

package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Objects;
import java.util.EmptyStackException;

/**
 * A {@link java.util.Stack}-like data structure to track all valid moves made by a player.
 *
 * <p>A stack is a data structure which enforces Last-In First-Out (LIFO) ordering of its elements.</p>
 *
 * <p>You can read more about stacks <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stack_(abstract_data_type)">here</a>.</p>
 */
public class MoveStack {

    @NotNull
    private final List<MoveResult> moves = new ArrayList<>();

    private int popCount = 0;

    /**
     * Peeks the topmost of the element of the stack.
     *
     * <p>
     * This method is intended for internal use only, although we will not stop you if you want to use this method in
     * your implementation.
     * </p>
     *
     * @return The instance of {@link MoveResult} at the top of the stack, corresponding to the last move performed by
     * the player.
     */
    public MoveResult peek() {
        if (moves.isEmpty()) {
            throw new EmptyStackException();
        }
        return moves.get(moves.size() - 1);
    }

    // Removed @Override here, since there's no supertype method to override.
    public void push(final MoveResult move) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(move, "move must not be null");
        popCount = 0;
        moves.add(move);
    }

    /**
     * @return Whether the stack is currently empty.
     */
    public boolean isEmpty() {
        return moves.isEmpty();
    }

    /**
     * Pops a move from this stack.
     *
     * @return The instance of {@link MoveResult} last performed by the player.
     * @throws java.util.EmptyStackException if there are no moves to pop.
     */
    public MoveResult pop() {
        if (moves.isEmpty()) {
            throw new EmptyStackException();
        }
        popCount++;
        return moves.remove(moves.size() - 1);
    }

    /**
     * @return The number of {@link MoveStack#pop} calls invoked.
     */
    public int getPopCount() {
        return popCount;
    }
}

Response Text:---
**Explanation (brief)**  
The compilation error  
```  
The method push(MoveResult) of type MoveStack must override or implement a supertype method  
```  
means that you have an `@Override` annotation on `push(...)` even though no superclass or interface declares a `push(MoveResult)` method. The fix is simply to remove the (now invalid) `@Override` annotation on `push(...)` so that the method no longer tries to override something that doesn’t exist.

---

```java
package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Objects;
import java.util.EmptyStackException;

/**
 * A {@link java.util.Stack}-like data structure to track all valid moves made by a player.
 *
 * <p>A stack is a data structure which enforces Last-In First-Out (LIFO) ordering of its elements.</p>
 *
 * <p>You can read more about stacks <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stack_(abstract_data_type)">here</a>.</p>
 */
public class MoveStack {

    @NotNull
    private final List<MoveResult> moves = new ArrayList<>();

    private int popCount = 0;

    /**
     * Peeks the topmost element of the stack.
     *
     * <p>
     * This method is intended for internal use only, although we will not stop you if you want to use this method in
     * your implementation.
     * </p>
     *
     * @return The instance of {@link MoveResult} at the top of the stack, corresponding to the last move performed by
     * the player.
     * @throws EmptyStackException if the stack is empty.
     */
    public MoveResult peek() {
        if (moves.isEmpty()) {
            throw new EmptyStackException();
        }
        return moves.get(moves.size() - 1);
    }

    /**
     * Pushes a move onto the stack.
     *
     * @param move the {@link MoveResult} to push; must not be null.
     * @throws NullPointerException if move is null.
     */
    public void push(final MoveResult move) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(move, "move must not be null");
        popCount = 0;
        moves.add(move);
    }

    /**
     * @return whether the stack is currently empty.
     */
    public boolean isEmpty() {
        return moves.isEmpty();
    }

    /**
     * Pops a move from this stack.
     *
     * @return The instance of {@link MoveResult} last performed by the player.
     * @throws EmptyStackException if there are no moves to pop.
     */
    public MoveResult pop() {
        if (moves.isEmpty()) {
            throw new EmptyStackException();
        }
        popCount++;
        return moves.remove(moves.size() - 1);
    }

    /**
     * @return The number of {@link #pop()} calls invoked.
     */
    public int getPopCount() {
        return popCount;
    }
}
```

package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Objects;
import java.util.EmptyStackException;

/**
 * A {@link java.util.Stack}-like data structure to track all valid moves made by a player.
 *
 * <p>A stack is a data structure which enforces Last-In First-Out (LIFO) ordering of its elements.</p>
 *
 * <p>You can read more about stacks <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stack_(abstract_data_type)">here</a>.</p>
 */
public class MoveStack {

    @NotNull
    private final List<MoveResult> moves = new ArrayList<>();

    private int popCount = 0;

    /**
     * Peeks the topmost element of the stack.
     *
     * <p>
     * This method is intended for internal use only, although we will not stop you if you want to use this method in
     * your implementation.
     * </p>
     *
     * @return The instance of {@link MoveResult} at the top of the stack, corresponding to the last move performed by
     * the player.
     * @throws EmptyStackException if the stack is empty.
     */
    public MoveResult peek() {
        if (moves.isEmpty()) {
            throw new EmptyStackException();
        }
        return moves.get(moves.size() - 1);
    }

    /**
     * Pushes a move onto the stack.
     *
     * @param move the {@link MoveResult} to push; must not be null.
     * @throws NullPointerException if move is null.
     */
    public void push(final MoveResult move) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(move, "move must not be null");
        popCount = 0;
        moves.add(move);
    }

    /**
     * @return whether the stack is currently empty.
     */
    public boolean isEmpty() {
        return moves.isEmpty();
    }

    /**
     * Pops a move from this stack.
     *
     * @return The instance of {@link MoveResult} last performed by the player.
     * @throws EmptyStackException if there are no moves to pop.
     */
    public MoveResult pop() {
        if (moves.isEmpty()) {
            throw new EmptyStackException();
        }
        popCount++;
        return moves.remove(moves.size() - 1);
    }

    /**
     * @return The number of {@link #pop()} calls invoked.
     */
    public int getPopCount() {
        return popCount;
    }
}

```java
/**
 * Creates an instance.
 *
 * <p>
```
```java
 * Note: Do NOT throw an exception when {@code numLives} is zero. This will be used in our testing.
 * </p>
 *
 * @param gameBoard The game board to be managed by this instance.
 * @param numLives  Number of lives the player has. If the value is negative, treat as if the player has an
 *                  unlimited number of lives.
```

```java
    if (numLives < 0) {

        this.numLives = numLives;
    }
    this.initialNumOfGems = gameBoard.countGems();
}
```

Response Text:---
**Explanation**

The game is considered lost exactly when the player has no remaining lives **and** the game does *not* use unlimited lives.  In our `GameState` class, unlimited lives is signaled by the constant `UNLIMITED_LIVES` (whose value is `-1`).  Therefore, `hasLost()` should return `true` precisely when `numLives` is not `UNLIMITED_LIVES` and is less than or equal to zero; otherwise it returns `false`.

---

```java
/**
 * Checks whether the game has been lost.
 *
 * <p>
 * The game is lost when the player has no lives remaining. For games which the player has unlimited lives, this
 * condition should never trigger.
 * </p>
 *
 * @return Whether the player has lost the game.
 */
public boolean hasLost() {
    // The game is lost if the player has a finite number of lives (i.e. not UNLIMITED_LIVES)
    // and those lives have been exhausted (numLives <= 0).
    return numLives != UNLIMITED_LIVES && numLives <= 0;
}
```
【F:pa1/model/GameState.java†L41-L59】

---

**Notes**

- We compare against `UNLIMITED_LIVES` to ensure that unlimited‑lives games never report lost.
- We check `numLives <= 0` so that even if lives somehow go negative, the game is still considered lost.
- This snippet can be dropped directly into your `GameState` class (Java 19).

Response Text:---
Below is a simple implementation of `increaseNumLives` that honours the “unlimited lives” sentinel ( `UNLIMITED_LIVES == -1` ).  If the player already has unlimited lives, it leaves `numLives` alone and returns `Integer.MAX_VALUE`; otherwise it adds `delta` to the current `numLives` and returns the updated value.

```java
/**
 * Increases the player's number of lives by the specified amount.
 *
 * @param delta The number of lives to give the player.
 * @return The new number of lives of the player. If the player has unlimited number of lives, returns
 * {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE}.
 */
public int increaseNumLives(final int delta) {
    if (numLives == UNLIMITED_LIVES) {
        // already unlimited → always report MAX_VALUE
        return Integer.MAX_VALUE;
    }
    // otherwise bump up the finite life‐count
    numLives += delta;
    return numLives;
}
```

```java
		this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard, "gameBoard must not be null");
		if (numLives < 0) {
			this.numLives = UNLIMITED_LIVES;
		} else {
			this.numLives = numLives;

		this.initialNumOfGems = gameBoard.countGems();
	}

	 */
	public boolean hasLost() {
		return numLives != UNLIMITED_LIVES && numLives <= 0;
```

```java
	 * @return  The new number of lives of the player. If the player has unlimited number of lives, returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE} .

	public int increaseNumLives(final int delta) {
		if (numLives == UNLIMITED_LIVES) {
			return Integer.MAX_VALUE;
		}
		numLives += delta;
		return numLives;
```

	 */
	public int decreaseNumLives(final int delta) {
		if (numLives == UNLIMITED_LIVES) {
			return Integer.MAX_VALUE;
		}
		numLives -= delta;
		return numLives;
```java
	}
```

Response Text:---
It looks like your `getScore()` needs to follow exactly the rules laid out in its Javadoc, but the repository doesn’t define a literal “gameBoardSize” field—instead you must derive it from the `GameBoard` API.  The simplest interpretation is that the initial score is the total number of squares on the board (rows × columns).  Then, at any point:

1. Base score = board‐size  
2. + 10 points × (initialNumOfGems − currentGems)  (i.e. gems collected so far)  
3. − 1 point × numMoves  
4. − 2 points × (moveStack.getNumUndos())  
5. − 4 points × numDeaths

Below is one correct implementation of `getScore()` that assumes your `GameBoard` exposes `getNumRows()` and `getNumCols()` (please adapt if your API differs).  It also uses `initialNumOfGems` (already stored in `GameState`) and assumes your `MoveStack` has a method `getNumUndos()` which returns how many undos have been performed.

```java
/**
 * <p>
 * At any point of the game, the score should be computed using the following formula:
 * </p>
 * <ul>
 * <li>The initial score of any game board is {@code gameBoardSize}.</li>
 * <li>Each gem will be worth 10 points.</li>
 * <li>Each valid move deducts one point.</li>
 * <li>Each undo deducts two points.</li>
 * <li>Each death deducts four points (on top of the one point deducted by a valid move).</li>
 * </ul>
 *
 * @return The current score of this game.
 */
public int getScore() {
    // 1. compute board size (rows * cols)
    int boardSize = gameBoard.getNumRows() * gameBoard.getNumCols();

    // 2. gems collected so far = initialNumOfGems - current gems remaining
    int gemsCollected = initialNumOfGems - gameBoard.countGems();

    // 3. points gained by collecting gems
    int gemPoints = gemsCollected * 10;

    // 4. move penalty
    int movePenalty = numMoves * 1;

    // 5. undo penalty (assumes MoveStack#getNumUndos())
    int undoPenalty = moveStack.getNumUndos() * 2;

    // 6. death penalty (note each death already decremented a move, but we add extra 3 more for 4 total)
    int deathPenalty = numDeaths * 4;

    // total
    return boardSize
         + gemPoints
         - movePenalty
         - undoPenalty
         - deathPenalty;
}
```

---

#### Explanation

- **Why wrap in a new view?**  
  The `GameBoardView` type (in package `pa1.view`) is designed so that clients can inspect the board without mutating it. By returning a fresh `GameBoardView(gameBoard)`, we ensure that callers cannot alter the real game state.
- **No caching needed.**  
  Since `GameBoardView` merely delegates to the underlying `GameBoard` in read‑only mode, creating a new instance on each call is cheap and guarantees isolation of references.

```java
	public int decrementNumLives() {

	}

	public int getScore() {

		int gemsCollected = initialNumOfGems - gameBoard.countGems();

		int movePenalty = numMoves * 1;
		int undoPenalty = moveStack.getNumUndos() * 2;
		int deathPenalty = numDeaths * 4;
		return boardSize + gemPoints - movePenalty - undoPenalty - deathPenalty;
```

```java
	 * @param gameBoard  The game board to be managed by this instance.
	 */
	public void GameState(final GameBoard gameBoard) {
		this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard, "gameBoard must not be null");
		this.numLives = UNLIMITED_LIVES;
		this.initialNumOfGems = gameBoard.countGems();
	}

	/**
	 * Creates an instance. <p> Note: Do NOT throw an exception when  {@code  numLives}  is zero. This will be used in our testing. </p>
	 * @param gameBoard  The game board to be managed by this instance.
	 * @param numLives   Number of lives the player has. If the value is negative, treat as if the player has an unlimited number of lives.
	 */
	public void GameState(final GameBoard gameBoard, final int numLives) {
		this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard, "gameBoard must not be null");
		if (numLives < 0) {
			this.numLives = UNLIMITED_LIVES;
		} else {
			this.numLives = numLives;
		}
		this.initialNumOfGems = gameBoard.countGems();
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether the game has been won. <p> The game is won when there are no gems left in the game board. </p>
	 * @return  Whether the player has won the game.
	 */
	public boolean hasWon() {
		return gameBoard.countGems() == 0;
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether the game has been lost. <p> The game is lost when the player has no lives remaining. For games which the player has unlimited lives, this condition should never trigger. </p>
	 * @return  Whether the player has lost the game.
	 */
	public boolean hasLost() {
		return numLives != UNLIMITED_LIVES && numLives <= 0;
	}

	 */
	public int increaseNumLives(final int delta) {
		if (numLives == UNLIMITED_LIVES) {
			return Integer.MAX_VALUE;
		}
		numLives += delta;
		return numLives;
	}

	public int decreaseNumLives(final int delta) {
```

```java
		this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard, "gameBoard must not be null");
		this.numLives = UNLIMITED_LIVES;
		this.initialNumOfGems = gameBoard.countGems();
	}

	/**
	 * Creates an instance. <p> Note: Do NOT throw an exception when  {@code  numLives}  is zero. This will be used in our testing. </p>
	 * @param gameBoard  The game board to be managed by this instance.
	 * @param numLives   Number of lives the player has. If the value is negative, treat as if the player has an unlimited number of lives.
	 */
	public void GameState(final GameBoard gameBoard, final int numLives) {
		this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard, "gameBoard must not be null");
		if (numLives < 0) {
			this.numLives = UNLIMITED_LIVES;
		} else {
			this.numLives = numLives;
		}
		this.initialNumOfGems = gameBoard.countGems();
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether the game has been won. <p> The game is won when there are no gems left in the game board. </p>
	 * @return  Whether the player has won the game.
	 */
	public boolean hasWon() {
		return gameBoard.countGems() == 0;
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether the game has been lost. <p> The game is lost when the player has no lives remaining. For games which the player has unlimited lives, this condition should never trigger. </p>
	 * @return  Whether the player has lost the game.
	 */
	public boolean hasLost() {
		return numLives != UNLIMITED_LIVES && numLives <= 0;
	}

	/**
	 * Increases the player's number of lives by the specified amount.
	 * @param delta  The number of lives to give the player.
	 * @return  The new number of lives of the player. If the player has unlimited number of lives, returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE} .
	 */
	public int increaseNumLives(final int delta) {
		if (numLives == UNLIMITED_LIVES) {
			return Integer.MAX_VALUE;
		}
		numLives += delta;
		return numLives;
	}

	/**
	 * Decreases the player's number of lives by the specified amount.
	 * @param delta  The number of lives to take from the player.
	 * @return  The new number of lives of the player. If the player has unlimited number of lives, returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE} .
	 */
	public int decreaseNumLives(final int delta) {
		if (numLives == UNLIMITED_LIVES) {
			return Integer.MAX_VALUE;
		}
		numLives -= delta;
		return numLives;
	}

	/**
	 * Decrements the player's number of lives by one.
	 * @return  The new number of lives of the player. If the player has unlimited number of lives, returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE} .
	 */
	public int decrementNumLives() {
		return decreaseNumLives(1);
	}

	/**
	 * Increments the number of moves taken by the player.
	 * @return  The new number of moves taken by the player.
	 */
	public int incrementNumMoves() {
		numMoves++;
		return numMoves;
	}

	/**
	 * Increments the number of deaths of the player.
	 * @return  The new number of deaths of the player.
	 */
	public int incrementNumDeaths() {
		numDeaths++;
		decrementNumLives();
		return numDeaths;
	}

	/**
	 * @return  The current number of deaths of the player.
	 */
	public int getNumDeaths() {
		return numDeaths;
	}

	/**
	 * @return  The current number of moves taken by the player.
	 */
	public int getNumMoves() {
		return numMoves;
	}

	/**
	 * @return  Whether the player has unlimited lives.
	 */
	public boolean hasUnlimitedLives() {
		return numLives == UNLIMITED_LIVES;
	}

	/**
	 * @return  The number of lives a player has. If the player has an unlimited number of lives, returns {@link Integer#MAX_VALUE} .
	 */
	public int getNumLives() {
		return (numLives == UNLIMITED_LIVES) ? Integer.MAX_VALUE : numLives;
	}

	/**
	 * @return  The number of gems that is still present on the game board.
	 */
	public int getNumGems() {
		return gameBoard.countGems();
	}

	/**
	 * <p> At any point of the game, the score should be computed using the following formula: </p> <ul> <li>The initial score of any game board is  {@code  gameBoardSize} .</li> <li>Each gem will be worth 10 points.</li> <li>Each valid move deducts one point.</li> <li>Each undo deducts two points.</li> <li>Each death deducts four points (on top of the one point deducted by a valid move).</li> </ul>
	 * @return  The current score of this game.
	 */
	public int getScore() {
		int boardSize = gameBoard.getNumRows() * gameBoard.getNumCols();
		int gemsCollected = initialNumOfGems - gameBoard.countGems();
		int gemPoints = gemsCollected * 10;
		int movePenalty = numMoves * 1;
		int undoPenalty = moveStack.getNumUndos() * 2;
		int deathPenalty = numDeaths * 4;
		return boardSize + gemPoints - movePenalty - undoPenalty - deathPenalty;
	}

	/**
	 * @return  A controller of the managed game board for mutation.
	 */
	public GameBoardController getGameBoardController() {
		return new GameBoardController(gameBoard);
	}

	/**
	 * @return  A read-only view of the managed game board.
	 */
	public GameBoardView getGameBoardView() {
		return new GameBoardView(gameBoard);
	}

	/**
	 * @return  The instance of the managed  {@link GameBoard} .
	 */
	public GameBoard getGameBoard() {
		return gameBoard;
	}
}
```
